issues.title: T74 follow-up: direct DOS wrapper proof ignores displaced return frames
issues.body:
Found during T74 / PR #393. This is a recorded limit outside ordinary ALL acceptance; the owner’s port priority remains unchanged (CLAUDE.md rule 23).

Static finding, with direct side-by-side proof reproduction still unverified: `235C:0000` moves its physical return frame by -2 bytes and falls through the `235C:000B` shared `retf 6` tail. T74 models this as `Entry.return_stack_delta=-2`, with actual synthetic Unicorn runner tests checking the caller PC/SP, register record, flags and shifted stack words. The effective argument cleanup is 4 bytes.

`port/prove.py` still predicts returns as `entry_sp + return_address_bytes + entry.pop` in its top-level call setup and nested-original return tracking (approximately lines 293 and 432 at ce8bc6dd). It omits the displacement: the far wrapper prediction is SP+10 while the actual return is SP+8. Do not claim direct DOS-wrapper `prove=` support from the successful runner tests. Shared-tail entry sequencing (0000 physically falling through registered 000B) may expose another proof issue and needs checking in the actual reproduction.

Ordinary ALL does not enter either DOS wrapper: the kit already supplies semantic keyboard services at 214B:0723/08DD. T74’s accepted mechanism for the wrappers is the actual IRET/registered-runner unit test; direct proof of these wrappers is an explicit known limit, documented in the kit README and T74 notes. Existing key-service self-answered proof refusals also remain.

Acceptance:
- Add a real synthetic registered-MSDOS side-by-side proof that fails before the fix; exercise top-level and nested displaced returns and shared-tail sequencing.
- Propagate return displacement through both proof return predictions, plus any sequencing correction the actual reproduction establishes.
- Preserve all existing proof assertions and ordinary zero-displacement behavior; run the existing guest/proof tests and demonstrate the new mutation controls fail.

No original executable bytes are required for the synthetic reproduction. Do not add masks, weaken stack comparisons, or spend a new port-task review loop on this edge before the port.

issues.title: T75/T76 unit tests miss three listing edges: position code 13, captain at slot 11, the 600-tick taker wait
issues.body:
**Severity**: SHOULD
**Found by**: milestone review #406 at `6342c48dda5c513dca8df39101475695134683fb` (against `m3-port-setup-tail`)

## What

Three edge mutations of T75/T76 port bodies pass `tests.test_port_selection` and `tests.test_port_takers` (25 tests). The port code matches the listing in all three places; only the tests are weak.

1. **`runtime/original_match/port/selection.py:322`:** `ss16(mem,r,r.bp-18)<=13` → `<=12` passes.
   - The listing at EC89 (`cmp word ptr [bp-0x12],0xd; ja`) loops over position codes 1..13, and 13 is a real code (F028).
   - The validity-warning test raises "more than 3" only at position 1, so the claim in `notes/T75.md` that unit tests cover each validity warning holds only for position 1.
2. **`runtime/original_match/port/takers.py:170`:** `ret='CCEC',…);bad=r.ax>11` → `>=11` passes.
   - The listing is `seg_0791_20.asm` CCEC `cmp ax,0xb` / CCEF `jbe`, so a captain at slot 11 is valid.
   - The review's fork also ran seven S matches with `--ports takers` on this mutant: all identical to the reference. So the integrated proof does not cover this edge either.
3. **`runtime/original_match/port/takers.py:101`:** `r.ax=600` → `601` (0BD0 `mov ax,0x258`, F030's 6 s nominal wait) passes.

## Reproduction

In a scratch copy, apply each single string replacement above, then run `python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_port_selection tests.test_port_takers`. Each gives `OK`.

## Why it matters

These are reached routines, but these exact edges are not visited by the 74-case corpus. A regression there would go unnoticed by both the units and ALL.

## Suggested fix (smallest)

Add three unit cases:
- four players at position code 13;
- a stored captain at slot 11;
- the 0B7C wait argument equal to 600.

**Effort**: S

— Milestone reviewer (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 `claude-opus-5-5`)

issues.title: T107 preregistration does not state its minimum detectable effect (needs block sum >= 24/32 per context)
issues.body:
**Severity**: SHOULD

**Found by: #455 at `c88461e9c2365de4c011a9df61f0523f1ec1a601`**

**What**
`docs/engine-study/experiment-budget.md:59-64` correctly computes the conservative per-context Hoeffding halfwidth 4·sqrt(ln 80 / 32) = 1.480 on the interaction I ∈ [−2, 2] with 16 blocks, and calls the result "probably inconclusive". It does not state the minimum detectable effect. Excluding zero needs Ī > 1.48 per context, i.e. a block sum ≥ 24 out of a maximum of 32 (≈ every block showing a positive interaction), or (Ī_A+Ī_B)/2 > 1.48 for the aggregate. With the retained F40 base rate (country 7 scored in 31/40 = 0.775), SD(I) is on the order of 0.8, so any plausible interaction has detection probability ≈ 0.

Note also that the equal-weight aggregate (the single primary estimand) admits a direct stratified Hoeffding bound over the 32 bounded block terms: halfwidth sqrt(0.5·ln 40 / 2) = 0.960 instead of averaging two 1.480 endpoints. That is still valid, conservative and fixed in advance, and it needs 1476 rather than 3506 blocks/context for ±0.1.

**Why it matters**
The primary analysis is preregistered. Readers should see before running that T107 cannot detect anything short of a near-maximal interaction, so that a null is not later read as "no effect". This is an honesty/precision disclosure; the method is not invalid.

**Suggested fix**
State the MDE explicitly (block sum ≥ 24/32 per context; aggregate mean > 1.48), and consider the direct aggregate bound. Decide before execution, not after.

**Effort**: S

— Milestone reviewer (Claude Code, claude-opus-5-5)


## Owner decision — 2026-10-27

The owner selected: **Defer T107 until the probe results inform a better design**. No existing T107 batch is authorised to execute. Complete bounded T106,then use its results to prepare a revised proposal before any match spending. Disclosure/threshold corrections were independently verified in ES-R2 round-two AGREE;this closes the spending question for the current preregistration without adopting the tighter bound or changing old records.

issues.body:
Part of #433, area 7 of the owner's ten-area engine study.

- **Difficulty:** hard; **Size:** M (2–4 plus separately capped compute active hours; compute separately capped).
- **Complexity:** high; **Impact:** medium.
- **Why these ratings:** Sampling, path divergence and context interactions make complexity high. Practical effect sizing is medium impact under the existing rubric.
- **Depends on:** T105 (#444), T106 (#445); ES-R2 (#455) accepted.
- **Planning brief:** `docs/tasks/T107.md`; programme: `docs/engine-study-plan.md`.

### Scope

Execute the first preregistered match batch on the validated path, with selected attribute/tactic contrasts, ordinary fixtures and declared context variation. Measure intermediate events as well as score, shots, possession, fouls, cards and energy. Publish results, including null or inconclusive effects, before considering more runs.

### Evidence

T105 preregistration, T106 controls, validated original/port execution path and T79 fidelity records when available.

### Acceptance

The batch respects its pinned design, cap and completion checks. Reproducible summaries give N, effect sizes/intervals, seed/context structure, failures and exploratory versus confirmatory labels. Deviations and further batches become separately scoped follow-ups.

### Hazards

Do not launch a large sweep because the plan exists, substitute quick results for watched play, treat common seeds as independent evidence, or claim equivalence from an inconclusive test.

### Dispatch gate

This records planned work; it does not start implementation. Split this 2–4-hour package into independently mergeable slices of about one hour before dispatch, using T95's census; keep this issue as their parent. Each executable contract must own its artifacts and have prechecked failing-on-baseline/passing-on-mock Done-when commands. Use static evidence first, retain immutable measurements, and obtain independent strong-model review for new game-rule claims. Production engine changes, original-bug fixes and backend changes are separate decisions/deliveries.

### Independent review gate

ES-R2 (#455) accepted. See [the review schedule](https://github.com/diegoami/goal2-archaeology/blob/main/docs/engine-study-reviews.md) for entry, review scope and exit criteria. 

### Owner-corrected implementation policy

- **Implementer:** the main session on `gpt-6.1-sol` at `high` performs this task directly.
- **Exceptional help:** use a `gpt-6.1-sol` / `xhigh` agent sparingly, only for the hardest narrowly scoped subproblem after working it at high. Do not delegate the whole task by default or treat a hard label as an automatic xhigh assignment.
- **Ceiling:** no Astra for implementation or review; no max/ultra escalation or automatic model/provider fallback. The previous mandatory per-task spawning and Claude implementation alternatives are superseded.
- **Independent review:** retain Claude or Kimi at the existing milestone. Select the actual reviewer model/settings at activation; the reviewer must not be an author. A Sol/xhigh helper does not supply the independent verdict.

Follow [the corrected main-session model policy](https://github.com/diegoami/goal2-archaeology/blob/main/docs/engine-study-models.md). Record the reason and narrow scope when exceptional help is used; the main session integrates and verifies the result. Existing dependencies, acceptance, evidence, compute-budget and prototype/review gates remain in force.
